aboutThanksText: Special thanks to Peña el Trompazo.
difficultySummary2: Gentle AI, but it starts punishing mistakes.
difficultySummary4: Demanding AI: saves strength and reads the table better.
difficultySummary5: Expert AI: barely wastes cards or bluffs.
difficultyCard1: May spend strong cards too early.
difficultyCard2: Sometimes rushes when it sees a chance.
difficultyCard3: Usually plays the cheapest useful winning card.
difficultyCard4: Saves strength and protects important rounds.
difficultyCard5: Optimizes card, turn and score precisely.
difficultyTruco1: Calls truco rarely and folds doubtful hands.
difficultyTruco2: Can call truco with clear support.
difficultyTruco3: Uses truco and raises with reasonable risk.
difficultyTruco4: Pressures with truco when it reads an edge.
difficultyTruco5: Raises, folds or bluffs with advanced reading.

tutorialObjectiveBody: You play with your partner against two rivals. Each hand scores points; the first team to 30 wins.
tutorialObjectivePrompt: Your partner sits opposite you. If your team controls the round, you should...
tutorialObjectiveAnswer: Good: Zapiti is won as a pair. Saving strong cards often decides the next round.
tutorialHandsBody: Each hand has up to three rounds. If a team wins two rounds, it wins the hand and scores its value.
tutorialHandsPrompt: If the rivals already won one round, the next one is for...
tutorialHandsAnswer: Exactly: when behind, win or tie with the cheapest useful card.
tutorialCardsBody: The highest number does not always win: the 4 of Clubs and the good sevens are very strong.
tutorialCardsPrompt: If you cannot win the table anymore, the best play is usually...
tutorialCardsAnswer: Right: a saved strong card can win later.
tutorialSignalsBody: You can ask your partner for a signal or give one yourself. Signals communicate strength without showing the card.
tutorialSignalsPrompt: Before accepting a doubtful truco, asking for a signal helps you...
tutorialSignalsAnswer: Exactly: the signal helps decide whether to save, accept, raise or pass.
tutorialTrucoBody: Calling truco raises the hand value. With strength you pressure; with a bluff you try to make rivals pass.
tutorialTrucoPrompt: A good bluff is made when...
tutorialTrucoAnswer: Good: a bluff works when the table and score make it believable.
tutorialPracticeBody: Now you will play real table situations with prepared cards.
tutorialPracticeAnswer: That's it. Enter practice and play each situation.
guidedCompleteInstruction: You have practiced cards, signals, truco, bluffing and passing.
guidedCompleteStatus: Tutorial completed. You have practiced cards, signals, truco, bluffing and passing.
guidedScenario1Instruction: Your partner is winning the table. Play the low card and save the Ace of Swords.
guidedScenario1Success: Well played: when your partner already controls, saving strength is gold.
guidedScenario2Instruction: The rival is winning. Beat it with the 3 and save the 7 of Cups.
guidedScenario2Success: Exactly: you used the lowest winning card and saved the big one.
guidedScenario3Instruction: The table is lost. Play the lowest card and save useful cards for later.
guidedScenario3Success: Good decision: when you cannot win, do not burn better cards.
guidedScenario4Instruction: Before risking it, ask for a signal: your partner can tell you what strength they hold.
guidedScenario4Success: Good read: with your partner's signal you can decide much more calmly.
guidedScenario5Instruction: You have the 4 of Clubs. Give that signal so your partner knows there is strength.
guidedScenario5Success: Perfect: a clear signal helps your partner save, accept or pressure.
guidedScenario6Instruction: You have a strong hand before playing. Call truco to raise the value.
guidedScenario6Success: Good: with real strength, calling truco before showing a card adds pressure.
guidedScenario7Instruction: You are weak, but the rivals see a doubtful table. Call truco as a bluff.
guidedScenario7Success: That is a useful bluff: not random, but made to pressure.
guidedScenario8Instruction: They call truco and you have nothing to fight with. Pass to lose less.
guidedScenario8Success: Correct: passing in time is also good play.

alVerBody: Your team has 29 points. You can play the hand or go home. If you go home, the rival team scores 2 points.
askCompanionSignalStatus: You ask your partner for a signal.
exitMatchBody: Are you sure you want to return to the menu? The current match will close.
tutorialFinePlayBody: If your partner already wins the table, play low. If you must win, use the lowest card that beats the rival.
tutorialFinePlayPrompt: Your partner is winning and you have a high card. The best move is...
tutorialFinePlayAnswer: That's it: do not burn a big card when the round is already controlled.
tutorialVoyMataTitle: I trust you and Kill it
tutorialVoyMataBody: I trust you asks your partner to try to win. Kill it is a stronger order: use it when you need to close.
tutorialVoyMataPrompt: If your partner cannot beat the table, they should...
tutorialVoyMataAnswer: Correct: if they cannot win, save strength for the next round.
tutorialAlVerBody: When a team is at 29 it is al ver. It can play the hand or go home and concede 2 points.
tutorialAlVerPrompt: You are al ver with a bad hand. Going home means...
tutorialAlVerAnswer: Exactly: you do not lose immediately, but you give the rival 2 points.
practiceSaveStrongSituation: Your partner wins the table. You can play low and save strength.
practiceSaveStrongFeedback: Correct: your team already controls, so you save the Ace of Swords for the next round.
practiceSaveRoundSituation: The rival is winning. If you can beat it, use the cheapest card.
practiceSaveRoundFeedback: Good: the 3 beats the 2. The 7 of Cups is saved for a harder round.
practiceBadTrucoSituation: They call truco, you have little game and the table already looks bad.
practiceBadTrucoFeedback: That's it: passing gives up less than accepting with no chances and losing more points.
practiceReadSignalSituation: Your partner shows strength. There is no need to rush your big card.
practiceReadSignalFeedback: Good read: with your partner's strong signal, you save the Ace for when it matters.
practiceAlVerSituation: You are at 29 with a bad hand. Playing may give the match away.
practiceAlVerFeedback: Correct: going home concedes 2 points, but avoids playing an almost lost hand.
